home.name: Francis Desjardins
home.breathing: Front-end infrastructure engineer · Breathing air since 1980.
home.enough: Prefers explicit over implicit, predictable over magical. Writes primitives other people build things with — which is either very useful or very humbling depending on the day. What a library refuses to do is the first decision, not the last.

skills.title: What I Build
skills.description: Framework-free cores with React, Solid and vanilla bindings over them. Zero runtime dependencies, three for three. Measures things in nanoseconds when nobody is watching.
skills.secondary: Also: a self-declared cat person. No further questions.

work.title: What's running
work.description: Two framework-agnostic libraries, each with its own playground. The names come from the three shadows an eclipse casts. What they refuse to do is documented as carefully as the rest.

dialog.name: antumbra
dialog.description: Dialog manager on the native top layer. Zero shipped UI: the renderer stays yours. React, Solid and vanilla bindings.

boot.name: umbra
boot.description: Bootstrap orchestrator. You declare what each step needs and the parallelism is derived from the graph — no flag, no concurrency ceiling.

designSystem.name: penumbra
designSystem.description: The design system both playgrounds wear — and the page that takes it apart, one layer at a time.

designSystem.title: Design system — Francis Desjardins
designSystem.description: penumbra, layer by layer: a scale with no colour, a palette with no brand, and a skin over it. Three layerings of the same specimen, switchable.
designSystem.ogTitle: The design system, layer by layer
designSystem.ogDescription: A scale with no colour, a palette with no brand, and what a project writes over them.

designSystem.title: The design system, layer by layer
designSystem.intro: penumbra ships two stylesheets and no brand. The first is scale, rhythm, motion and stacking, with no colour in it at all. The second is colour, and carries only what every project needs and none of them decides differently. What is left for a project to write is a typeface and eight names — or, if it would rather, all of it.

base.name: The base alone
base.note: Nothing over it. No typeface is declared and neither are the eight brand names, so the type falls back to the browser’s own faces and the filled button to the text ink. This is what a project has before it writes a line of its own.

tint.name: A tint over it
tint.note: Eleven declarations: three typefaces and the eight colours a project paints itself with. The surfaces, the three text ranks, the divider, the control edge, the states, the four semantics, the scrim and the lift are all still the base’s. This is the shape both playgrounds use.

replaced.name: The base replaced
replaced.note: No base at all. This skin declares the 24 neutral and semantic names itself, so the only thing left of the package is the scale. Light mode is dark here, elevation is a hard edge rather than a soft lift, and every face is monospaced — and not one line of the specimen below changed.

specimen.title: One card, nothing else
specimen.body: The same markup in all three states: every value in it is a variable, and there is no literal and no branch on the colour scheme.
specimen.secondary: Secondary text, one rank down — the rank a caption or a hint is written in.
specimen.caption: Switch the page between light and dark: each state answers for both.
